command:
cd $WORKSPACE_PATH && git commit -m "$(cat <<'COMMITMSG'
Relocate orphaned single-hit mesh move plans even without a citing wiki link

`wiki check --fix` could report a fully clean run while a mesh anchor stayed permanently STALE in `wiki mesh show` — reported on card main-1, reproduced by `plan_mesh_follows_orphans_single_hit_move_without_citing_link` in the prior commit. The gap: [`plan_mesh_follows`](packages/cli/src/commands/check_fix.rs#L1409-L1651) computes a `MeshMovePlan` whenever a stale anchor's content is found at exactly one other location, but the only code that ever applied one — `store::relocate_anchor` inside Fix #2's per-wiki-page link loop — only ran when some markdown href literally cited the plan's exact old `(path, start, end)`. Mesh anchors don't have to correspond to a literal link (they can encode code-to-code couplings), so any plan without a citing link fell through every path: never relocated, never counted toward `anchor_stale_count`, never diagnosed by bare `check` (which only reads `outcome.drifted`).

The fix adds a "Fix #2c" pass in [`run_fix_pass`](packages/cli/src/commands/check_fix.rs#L2495-L2534) that walks the full `move_plans` vector — not just the subset a link loop happens to touch — and calls `store::relocate_anchor` for every one of them. Because `relocate_anchor` looks an anchor up by its old coordinates and silently no-ops once those coordinates no longer exist, re-running it over plans the link loop already applied costs nothing; the pass simply converges the mesh's stored state unconditionally. Successful relocations get folded into the existing `anchor_refresh_applied` bookkeeping so they're staged the same way a whitespace-only hash refresh already is — consistent with this file's existing philosophy that a confidently single-hit move is corrected silently rather than surfaced as a finding.

command:
cd $WORKSPACE_PATH && git commit -m "$(cat <<'COMMITMSG'
Reconcile pre-existing wiki mesh drift blocking yarn validate

`yarn validate` runs `wiki check` against this repo's own `.wiki/` meshes as part of the release-binary smoke step, and it was failing independently of the [check_fix.rs](packages/cli/src/commands/check_fix.rs) work in the prior two commits — confirmed by reproducing the same failures against the pre-fix baseline tag. Several meshes anchored source ranges (`mesh_coverage.rs`, `git-mesh-usage.md`) that had drifted with meaning-changing edits since they were last anchored, and two meshes (`wiki/meta/operator-facing-documentation`, `wiki/meta/update-order`) still cited `CLAUDE.md#L83-L94`, a wiki-instructions section that commit e3733ff3's full rewrite of [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) removed outright rather than moved — the section no longer exists anywhere in the file.

Per the golden rule, an unrelated pre-existing validation failure still has to be resolved rather than waved off, so this re-hashes the genuinely-drifted anchors with `wiki mesh add` (acknowledging their current content), removes the two now-permanently-dead `CLAUDE.md#L83-L94` anchors with `wiki mesh remove`, and updates [wiki/meta/wiki-documentation-touchpoints.md](wiki/meta/wiki-documentation-touchpoints.md) — which directly linked the same dead range twice — to stop pointing operators at wiki instructions that CLAUDE.md no longer carries. `wiki check --fix` then scaffolded fresh coverage for the touched "Update Order" section automatically.

`wiki check` and full `yarn validate` both exit 0 after this commit.
COMMITMSG
)"

# Benchmark: anchor-cache cold vs warm economy

The Phase 5 evidence run measures what the anchor cache eliminates from `wiki check`: the `--anchor-cache` mode of [bench.mjs](/packages/cli/scripts/bench.mjs) wipes the cache, times one cold check, then five warm ones, and decomposes each run into the `cache.fingerprint` + `cache.walk` span sums (`legMs`) parsed from `wiki.log`.

## Setup

- Binary: release build from source under test (`packages/cli/target/build/release/wiki`, 0.5.111).
- Real corpus: this repository, 721 commits, ~40 wiki pages with line-range links.
- Synthetic corpus: generated by the same mode — 10,000 fast-import commits alternating two target blobs whose cited range (L1-L3) never changes, plus one constant page with `links-reviewed: 1`, so the check stays Healthy while the anchor walk blob-reads the page at every walked commit.
- Filesystem: fuse (hostile class — numbers are a distribution, not a scoreboard).

## Results (three measurement passes)

Real corpus — cold cache-leg sum: **4048.3 / 3080.7 / 3594.8 ms** (median ≈ 3.6 s); warm: **0.0 ms in all 15 warm runs** (wall medians 2989 / 2999 / 3124 ms — the uncacheable floor: the always-running `git log` capture, index prep, and classification). Warm serving is exact: 76 fingerprint hits + 7 walk hits, zero misses — every row served, nothing recomputed.

Synthetic 10k-commit corpus — cold legs 8.5 / 4.5 / 4.6 ms → warm 0.0 ms.

## What it shows

The warm path pays none of the memoized cost on either corpus. The real corpus's ~3.6 s cold legs are the O(commits × pages) history cost the card cites; the synthetic corpus's ~5 ms shows the in-process per-commit blob read itself is cheap (~0.5 µs/read) — the real cost lives in the per-commit tree-diff work the `--follow` log machinery pays on a large tree, which is exactly why the log capture must stay uncacheable (it always runs) while the memoized per-commit leg van...
